nodes.summary: A multi-marked Dyck path $P$ has a marked tail when its final run of vertical steps (the steps after its last horizontal step $E$, or all of $P$ if $P$ has no step $E$) contains a marked vertical step $N^*_t$ for some index $t \ge 2$.
nodes.title: Marked tail

nodes.summary: A multi-marked Dyck path $P$ has an unmarked tail when it does not have a marked tail, that is, when its final run of vertical steps (the steps after its last horizontal step $E$, or all of $P$ if $P$ has no step $E$) contains no marked vertical step.
nodes.title: Unmarked tail

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a marked Dyck path with $\ell$ steps. For a position $i$ with $0 \le i < \ell$, the step of $P$ at position $i$ is marked when it is the marked vertical step $N^*$ (rather than an unmarked vertical step $N$ or a horizontal step $E$).
nodes.title: Marked step of a marked Dyck path

nodes.summary: For a finite sequence $P$ of marked Dyck steps, $E(P)$ is the number of horizontal steps $E$ in $P$.
nodes.title: Number of horizontal steps in a marked Dyck step sequence

nodes.summary: For a finite sequence $P$ of marked Dyck steps, $N(P)$ is the number of unmarked vertical steps $N$ in $P$.
nodes.title: Number of unmarked vertical steps

nodes.summary: For a finite sequence $P$ of marked Dyck steps, $N^*(P)$ is the number of marked vertical steps $N^*$ in $P$.
nodes.title: Number of marked vertical steps

nodes.summary: Let $E(Q)$, $N(Q)$ and $N^*(Q)$ denote the numbers of horizontal steps $E$, unmarked vertical steps $N$ and marked vertical steps $N^*$ in a finite sequence $Q$ of marked Dyck steps. A marked Dyck path is a finite sequence $P$ of marked Dyck steps such that $E(P) = N(P) + N^*(P)$ and every prefix $Q$ of $P$ satisfies $N(Q) + N^*(Q) \le E(Q)$: a lattice path from $(0, 0)$ that ends on the diagonal and never goes…
nodes.title: Marked Dyck path

nodes.summary: A step of a marked Dyck path is one of three kinds: a horizontal step $E = (1, 0)$, an unmarked vertical step $N = (0, 1)$, or a marked vertical step $N^* = (0, 1)$.
nodes.title: Steps of a marked Dyck path

nodes.summary: For a finite sequence $P$ of multi-marked steps (horizontal steps $E$, plain vertical steps $N$ and marked vertical steps $N^*_t$ with index $t \ge 2$), $E(P)$ is the number of horizontal steps $E$ in $P$.
nodes.title: Number of horizontal steps in a multi-marked step sequence

nodes.summary: For every multi-marked Dyck path $P$, the number $E(P)$ of horizontal steps of $P$ equals the number of vertical steps of $P$, plain steps $N$ and marked steps $N^*_t$ counted together.
nodes.title: Equal horizontal and vertical step counts

nodes.summary: For a finite sequence $P$ of multi-marked steps (horizontal steps $E$, plain vertical steps $N$ and marked vertical steps $N^*_s$ with index $s \ge 2$) and a natural number $t$, $N^*_t(P)$ is the number of marked steps in $P$ whose index is exactly $t$.
nodes.title: Number of marked steps of a given index

nodes.summary: For a finite sequence $P$ of multi-marked steps (horizontal steps $E$, plain vertical steps $N$ and marked vertical steps $N^*_t$ with index $t \ge 2$), $N(P)$ is the number of plain (unmarked) vertical steps $N$ in $P$.
nodes.title: Number of plain vertical steps

nodes.summary: For a finite sequence $P$ of multi-marked steps (horizontal steps $E$, plain vertical steps $N$ and marked vertical steps $N^*_t$ with index $t \ge 2$), this is the total number of steps in $P$, that is, the length of $P$.
nodes.title: Number of steps

nodes.summary: For a finite sequence $P$ of multi-marked steps (horizontal steps $E$, plain vertical steps $N$ and marked vertical steps $N^*_t$ with index $t \ge 2$), this is the number of vertical steps in $P$, plain steps $N$ and marked steps $N^*_t$ counted together.
nodes.title: Number of vertical steps

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $\tilde P_n$ is the set of multi-marked Dyck paths $P$ of size $n$. Here the size of $P$ is $E(P) + \sum (t - 1)$, where $E(P)$ is the number of horizontal steps of $P$ and the sum runs over the marked steps $N^*_t$ of $P$, each occurrence counted separately.
nodes.title: Multi-marked Dyck paths of a given size

nodes.summary: A multi-marked Dyck path is a finite sequence $P$ of steps, each a horizontal step $E = (1,0)$, a plain vertical step $N = (0,1)$ or a marked vertical step $N^*_t = (0,1)$ carrying an index $t \ge 2$, such that every prefix of $P$, including the empty prefix and $P$ itself, has at most as many vertical steps (plain and marked) as horizontal steps, and $P$ has exactly as many vertical steps as horizontal steps.
nodes.title: Multi-marked Dyck path

nodes.summary: For a finite sequence $s$ of steps of a multi-marked Dyck path, the index sum of $s$ is the sum of the indices $t$ over all occurrences of marked steps $N^*_t$ in $s$, each occurrence counted separately; the steps $E$ and $N$ contribute nothing.
nodes.title: Index sum of a multi-marked step sequence

nodes.summary: A step of a multi-marked Dyck path is vertical when it is the plain step $N$ or a marked step $N^*_t$; the horizontal step $E$ is not vertical. This test delimits the final run of vertical steps of a step sequence.
nodes.title: Vertical steps of a multi-marked Dyck path

nodes.summary: For a finite sequence $s$ of steps of a multi-marked Dyck path, the shifted index sum of $s$ is the sum of $t - 1$ over all occurrences of marked steps $N^*_t$ in $s$, each occurrence counted separately; the steps $E$ and $N$ contribute nothing.
nodes.title: Shifted index sum of a multi-marked step sequence

nodes.summary: For every multi-marked Dyck path $P$, the size $E(P) + \sum (t - 1)$ of $P$ equals $N(P) + \sum t$, where $E(P)$ is the number of horizontal steps $E$ of $P$, $N(P)$ is the number of plain vertical steps $N$ of $P$, and both sums run over all occurrences of marked steps $N^*_t$ in $P$.
nodes.title: Two expressions for the size of a multi-marked Dyck path

nodes.summary: The size of a finite sequence $s$ of steps of a multi-marked Dyck path is $E(s) + \sum (t - 1)$, where $E(s)$ is the number of horizontal steps $E$ in $s$ and the sum runs over all occurrences of marked steps $N^*_t$ in $s$.
nodes.title: Size of a multi-marked step sequence

nodes.summary: A step of a multi-marked Dyck path is one of the horizontal step $E = (1, 0)$, the plain vertical step $N = (0, 1)$, or, for an integer $t \ge 2$, the marked vertical step $N^*_t = (0, 1)$ of index $t$. There are no marked steps of index less than $2$.
nodes.title: Steps of a multi-marked Dyck path

nodes.summary: The final run of vertical steps of a finite sequence $s$ of steps of a multi-marked Dyck path is the longest suffix of $s$ consisting of vertical steps ($N$ or $N^*_t$): the part of $s$ after its last horizontal step $E$, or all of $s$ if $s$ has no step $E$.
nodes.title: Final run of vertical steps

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $\tilde R_n$ is the set of multi-marked Dyck paths of size $n$ with an unmarked tail, that is, whose final run of vertical steps contains no marked step.
nodes.title: Multi-marked Dyck paths with an unmarked tail

nodes.summary: For every finite sequence $s$ of steps of a multi-marked Dyck path, the number of vertical steps of $s$ plus the shifted index sum of $s$ equals the number of plain vertical steps $N$ of $s$ plus the index sum of $s$.
nodes.title: Vertical count plus shifted index sum

nodes.summary: The size of a marked Dyck path $P$ is $N^*(P) + E(P)$, where $N^*(P)$ is the number of marked vertical steps of $P$ and $E(P)$ the number of its horizontal steps.
nodes.title: Size of a marked Dyck path

nodes.summary: For every marked Dyck path $P$, the size of $P$ equals $N(P) + 2N^*(P)$, where $N(P)$ and $N^*(P)$ are the numbers of unmarked and marked vertical steps of $P$.
nodes.title: Size of a marked Dyck path in vertical steps

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
